title: The Six Orthodox Schools: Systems of Vedic Philosophy

questions.question: What makes a school 'astika' or orthodox?
options: Belief in a personal creator God
Acceptance of the Vedas as a valid source of knowledge
questions.rationale: Astika schools accept the Vedas as pramana. Samkhya and early Mimamsa are astika yet lack a creator God.

questions.question: Match the school with its founder: Vaisheshika is attributed to:
questions.rationale: Kanada founded Vaisheshika (atomism, seven padarthas); Gautama founded Nyaya, Kapila Samkhya, and Jaimini Mimamsa.

questions.question: Which pramanas does Nyaya admit?
questions.rationale: Nyaya's four pramanas are pratyaksha, anumana, upamana, and shabda; inference is laid out in five steps.

questions.question: The seven padarthas — including substance, quality, action, generality, particularity, inherence, and non-existence — belong to:
questions.rationale: Kanada's Vaisheshika catalogues everything knowable under seven categories, including abhava (non-existence) added by followers.

questions.question: Samkhya's dualism is between:
questions.rationale: Purusha is passive, countless consciousness; prakriti is the one active material source. Liberation (kaivalya) is discriminating the two.

questions.question: The three gunas of Samkhya are:
questions.rationale: Prakriti's strands are sattva (lucidity), rajas (energy), and tamas (inertia); their disturbed equilibrium unfolds the 23 evolutes.

questions.question: Patanjali's Yoga Sutras define yoga as:
options: The cessation of the fluctuations of the mind
questions.rationale: Yogash chitta-vritti-nirodhah — yoga is stilling the mind's fluctuations, achieved through the eight limbs from yama to samadhi.

questions.question: The doctrine of apaurusheyatva, defended by Mimamsa, holds that:
options: The Vedas are not the work of any author and so cannot be false
questions.rationale: For Jaimini's school the Vedas are eternal and authorless — hence self-valid (svatah pramanya), needing no external confirmation.

questions.question: 'Purva Mimamsa' and 'Uttara Mimamsa' are the earlier and later inquiries — the latter is better known as:
questions.rationale: Vedanta ('the end of the Vedas') is Uttara Mimamsa, systematised in Badarayana's Brahmasutras, which begins from the Upanishads rather than ritual injunctions.

questions.question: Which school counts exactly 25 tattvas in its map of reality?
questions.rationale: Samkhya's 25 tattvas run from prakriti through intellect, ego, mind, senses, subtle and gross elements, up to purusha. Yoga accepts the same map plus Ishvara.
